title: What If Wolves Vanished From Yellowstone?

scenes.text: What if wolves vanished from Yellowstone? They did, and scientists still argue about what changed.
Hunters, trappers and poisoners wiped out the park's wolves by the nineteen twenties.
Without predators, elk climbed to about twenty thousand by the mid-nineteen-eighties and overgrazed the northern range.
Along the Lamar River, researchers found almost no young cottonwoods between seedlings and trees about seventy years old.
Forty-one wolves were released from 1995 to 1997. Elk began avoiding streambeds, and taller willows and cottonwoods returned at six of eight study sites.
But the viral story is too simple. Later studies found aspen recovery much weaker, and scientists still debate how big the wolf effect really is.

description:
What if wolves vanished from Yellowstone?
They did, for about 70 years. Elk boomed to around 20,000, young trees stopped growing, and the return of wolves in 1995 is still being studied.
